article.title: The Khata & Compass Journal
article.description: Mahesh Gowda's (39) hunt for a third plot on the Doddaballapur–Devanahalli arc — A-khata or DC-converted only, EC traced 30 years, and boundaries verified by a surveyor's ₹15K habit, not a seller's confidence.

tabs.title: Who he is
tabs.description: Getting to know Mahesh Gowda (39, sales director at an agri-inputs company) — a Mandya farming-family purist who owns zero apartments by conviction and is hunting a third plot on the north-Bengaluru STRR/airport arc.

buyers.name: Mahesh Gowda
buyers.description: From a Mandya farming family, owns zero apartments by conviction. Runs his plot thesis like a field officer — driving corridors himself, photographing road-widening markers, and auditing his own 2018 corridor predictions annually. Scorns apartments, but his discipline is real.

tabs.sharedVisionDescription: Never sell mud, never buy depreciation. A third A-khata plot on the north corridor where the next decade's appreciation lives — bought at launch, verified to the boundary stone, and held as the family's appreciating inheritance rather than a depreciating home.

tabs.insightTitle: What I noticed while we were searching
tabs.insightDescription: “Mahesh didn't want my opinion on which corridor. He wanted me to run his own numbers back at him — of the five corridors he believed in in 2018, two delivered, one half-delivered, two are still PowerPoints. So we didn't kill the thesis; we sized the bet down like a man who's been forty percent wrong before. The plot shrank from 2,400 to 1,500 sqft, and the difference became a flat deposit.”

chatMessages.text: Nodi Riya, fifteen thousand I paid that surveyor, and he tells me the boundary is three feet inside. Three feet! The seller's map was showing full confidence, guru.
Confidence is free, Mahesh. Boundaries cost fifteen thousand. You just saved yourself a plot you'd have fought over for ten years.

tabs.name: Learnings
tabs.label: Learnings
tabs.title: What this journey teaches us.
tabs.description: Key takeaways for plot buyers who believe land outlasts buildings, on the north-Bengaluru corridor.

lessons.title: The cheapest report in real estate is the one before registration.
lessons.description: A ₹15K private survey found a 3-foot boundary discrepancy the layout map didn't show. The deal died at the sketch stage; the habit was born for every plot after.
lessons.imagegenerationprompt: A 3D vector illustration of a surveyor's sketch with a 3-foot boundary discrepancy hatched in red beside a GPS-pinned boundary-stone photo, rendered in an 80% greyscale monochrome palette (#1E1E1E to #FFFFFF) with a Warm Coral #FF8A65 hatch accent, Scandinavian minimalism, clean white background, editorial quality.

lessons.title: Launch-day pricing is where a plot buyer's edge actually lives.
lessons.description: First-allotment rates at credible plotted developments ran 10–15% below month-six broker pricing. The edge was never 'finding undervalued corners' — it was being at launch.
lessons.imagegenerationprompt: A 3D vector illustration of a launch-morning price sheet with a first-allotment receipt and a corner-plot pick slip, rendered in an 80% greyscale monochrome palette (#1E1E1E to #FFFFFF) with a Warm Coral #FF8A65 launch-price accent, Scandinavian minimalism, clean white background, editorial quality.

lessons.title: Tendered infrastructure is a gate; proposed infrastructure is a treasure map.
lessons.description: A ₹3,900/sqft 'STRR-junction' pre-launch died the moment the junction turned out to be a proposal, not a tender. Base-rate discipline decides which corridors get capital.
lessons.imagegenerationprompt: A 3D vector illustration of an STRR pre-launch flyer with 'proposal ≠ tender' written across it in field pencil beneath a roadmap marker, rendered in an 80% greyscale monochrome palette (#1E1E1E to #FFFFFF) with a Warm Coral #FF8A65 pencil accent, Scandinavian minimalism, clean white background, editorial quality.

lessons.title: Liquidity is the tax land charges for its purity.
lessons.description: His Bidadi exit closed 14 months after listing, 11% below his anchor price. Every future plot is now sized against what 'selling fast' really means.
lessons.imagegenerationprompt: A 3D vector illustration of a land sale timeline graph spanning 14 months with a price anchor marked 11% below target, rendered in an 80% greyscale monochrome palette (#1E1E1E to #FFFFFF) with a Warm Coral #FF8A65 anchor-line accent, Scandinavian minimalism, clean white background, editorial quality.

beforeItems.text: Land appreciation is about finding the undervalued corner no one else sees
A 10-15% launch discount is a bonus, not the core thesis
The layout map and the seller's word are enough before registration
Every government road announcement is a buy signal worth chasing

afterItems.text: Base-rate discipline beats discovery — buy approved layouts at launch, sized to your own 40% miss rate
Launch-day first-allotment pricing is the entire edge; broker pricing by month six is 10–15% higher
A ₹15K private survey and a tendered-vs-proposed filter gate every rupee
Position-size the plot against liquidity — and leave room for the family's home the thesis almost forgot

differentlyCards.title: Run the base-rate audit in month one
differentlyCards.description: Of the five corridors he believed in in 2018, only two delivered. Auditing his own miss rate earlier would have resized every position from the start.

differentlyCards.title: Chase launch windows ahead of the corridor
differentlyCards.description: The STRR-teaser detour cost three weeks because he followed a proposal; staying on credible launch-calendars only would have saved it entirely.

differentlyCards.title: Order the ₹15K survey before love,
differentlyCards.description: Running verification before falling for a favourite site would have saved the two-week grief of the 3-foot kill.

differentlyCards.title: Have the home-upgrade conversation earlier
differentlyCards.description: His wife had stopped mentioning the bigger house entirely. Holding that conversation in month two — not month six — changed the plot size with far less tension.

differentlyCards.title: Price liquidity into every purchase
differentlyCards.description: The Bidadi exit's 14 months and 11% haircut should have been a headline line-item in every plot's internal rate, not a lesson learned at the exit.

tabs.adviceDescription: For plot buyers on the north corridor, the honest move is to buy A-khata or DC-converted land at launch — where first-allotment pricing beats month-six by 10–15% — gate every rupee behind a tendered-vs-proposed filter and a ₹15K private survey, and position-size against your own base rate. Mahesh proved the thesis could carry one smaller plot and still make room for the family's home.

checklistItems: You believe buildings depreciate and land doesn't, and you hold this as identity, not just analysis.
You drive corridors on weekends and photograph road-widening markers for fun.
Your family's wealth story began (or broke) with a land decision, and it still drives you.
You'd walk away at the registration table if one document smelled wrong — and you have.
Your entire net worth rides one thesis, and you've never computed its failure case aloud.
Someone at home wants a bigger house now, and your plots are the reason there isn't one.
